title: Coral Tissue and Skeleton Separation for DNA and RNA Extraction
author: Molly A Moynihan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bi4ykgxw
materials: Funnels should be washed and re-autoclaved before reuse.

steps.title: Prepare PBS‑EDTA airbrush solution
steps.instruction: Add 5.84 mg EDTA to 2 L 1× PBS to obtain 10 µM EDTA; filter‑sterilize 30–50 mL aliquots through a 0.22 µm syringe filter into sterile nuclease‑free Falcon/Corning tubes and keep them closed until use.

steps.title: Set up airbrushing workspace
steps.instruction: Designate a laboratory area separate from molecular work to avoid aerosol contamination; clean the acrylic box, bench, and equipment with bleach, ethanol, and RNaseZap; place a small insulated bowl filled with dry ice and an upright labeled Falcon tube in contact with the dry ice (use 50 mL Falcon/Corning tubes if the homogenizer probe must fit).

steps.title: Prepare funnel and airbrush
steps.instruction: Autoclave a funnel (8–16 recommended), spray with RNaseZap, rinse with nuclease‑free water, dry with compressed air, and place the funnel inside the Falcon tube and inside the acrylic box; connect the airbrush to a compressed‑air source, fill with nuclease‑free water and purge the water out the front end.

steps.title: Prepare cryopulverizer workspace
steps.instruction: Fill one styrofoam box with liquid nitrogen (LN₂) for the cryopulverizer and another with dry ice for sample storage; clean tweezers, bench top, and the cryopulverizer with ethanol and RNaseZap, rinse with nuclease‑free water, and thoroughly dry with Kim wipes; place the cryopulverizer in LN₂ and allow it to cool for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Retrieve coral sample
steps.instruction: Remove the coral sample from dry ice/LN₂; if needed, break it into smaller pieces with a sterilized chisel, keeping remaining pieces on dry ice/LN₂ or at –80 °C; place the piece to be processed inside the prepared funnel.

steps.title: Airbrush tissue from skeleton
steps.instruction: Pour 3–5 mL of the 0.22 µm‑filtered, autoclaved PBS solution into the airbrush (close the PBS tube immediately after); hold the sample with sterilized tweezers above the funnel inside the acrylic box and spray PBS to detach coral tissue, collecting the tissue in the Falcon tube; use additional PBS as needed for larger fragments.

steps.title: Collect skeleton after airbrushing
steps.instruction: Transfer the remaining skeletal fragment to a clean Falcon tube and store the tube in LN₂ or on dry ice.

steps.title: Homogenize airbrushed tissue
steps.instruction: Remove the Falcon tube containing tissue from dry ice and homogenize the tissue for approximately 5 seconds with the tissue homogenizer probe.

steps.title: Prepare skeleton for pulverization
steps.instruction: Cover the tissue‑free skeletal fragment in LN₂ by adding a small volume of LN₂ to the Falcon tube or by placing the fragment in a small insulated dish containing LN₂.

steps.title: Pulverize skeleton
steps.instruction: Remove the cryopulverizer from LN₂, place the frozen skeleton into the pulverizer using tweezers, and strike the pulverizer repeatedly with a mallet until the material becomes a fine powder.

steps.title: Clean tissue homogenizer
steps.instruction: Rinse the homogenizer sequentially in three beakers of Elga water, briefly turn it on in the water, unscrew the outer probe, spray with ethanol, clean with RNaseZap, rinse with nuclease‑free water, then fill a clean Falcon tube with a few mL nuclease‑free water and run the homogenizer briefly in the tube; repeat until no foaming is observed.

steps.title: Clean cryopulverizer (replicate samples)
steps.instruction: While still frozen, wipe the interior and exterior of the pulverizer thoroughly with Kim wipes using tweezers; reassemble the two pieces and keep the pulverizer in LN₂ to stay cold.

steps.title: Clean cryopulverizer (different sample type)
steps.instruction: Thaw the pulverizer in a drying oven at 50–60 °C, then place it in an ultrasonicator for ~5 minutes to remove residual powder; clean with ethanol, RNaseZap, and nuclease‑free water; dry completely and return to LN₂ before the next use.

steps.title: Clean airbrush, chisel, and tools
steps.instruction: Clean the airbrush and chisel with ethanol and RNaseZap, rinse with nuclease‑free water, and purge the airbrush with nuclease‑free water; also rinse the tissue homogenizer, cryopulverizer, and any other tools with ethanol and RNaseZap, then rinse thoroughly with nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Store cleaned funnels
steps.instruction: Autoclave 8–16 funnels and store them in a container that has been cleaned with bleach, ethanol, and RNaseZap.

steps.title: Prepare samples for extraction
steps.instruction: Retrieve frozen coral samples from the –80 °C freezer and place them on dry ice or LN₂; work with two people (one airbrushing, one pulverizing) to process 16–20 samples per day.

steps.title: Aliquot tissue for DNA/RNA
steps.instruction: Using filter‑pipette tips, dispense the airbrushed tissue into microcentrifuge or extraction tubes, making at least two 200–500 µL aliquots for DNA and RNA and an additional 1–2 mL backup; for RNA, tissue may be placed directly into Trizol and stored at –80 °C (vortex before freezing), although higher yields are obtained by freezing tissue first and adding Trizol on the day of extraction.

steps.title: Aliquot skeleton for DNA/RNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the powdered skeleton into 2–3 microcentrifuge tubes (≈0.2–0.5 cm³ per tube) for DNA and RNA extraction and a backup tube; for RNA, the skeleton can be placed directly into Trizol, adding 1–5 µL of 6 M HCl per 1 mL Trizol; higher yields are achieved by freezing the skeletal aliquot first and adding Trizol later.

steps.title: Label and store aliquots
steps.instruction: Pre‑label six microcentrifuge tubes per coral sample and two Falcon tubes for temporary holding; immediately place all tissue and skeleton aliquots on dry ice or in a dry shipper/LN₂ and store at –80 °C until extraction.
